To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

finite difference frequency-domain methods can be applied to the analysis of electromagnetic waves in the presence of metamaterials without any modification, while finite-element frequency-domain methods require special modifications.
the finite difference method does not suffer of the same inconvenient as the finite element method in the presence of an effective medium.

(a) the accuracy of FDTD method is not affected in the presence of the effective models; (b) the reason for this is that the FDTD method uses only the electric field and its derivatives in the discretized equations, and the effective model is only related to the electric field; (c) on the other hand, the FEM method requires the magnetic field as well, and the effective models are related to both electric and magnetic fields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical solution of Maxwell’s equations for the design of metamaterials with negative refractive index.
the analysis of the finite difference time domain (FDTD) and finite difference frequency domain (FDFD) methods in the presence of metamaterials and effective models thereof.
the development of numerical methods to solve Maxwell equations in the frequency domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FDFD method is the most suitable method for the numerical analysis of metamaterials in the frequency domain.
, in the presence of metamaterials, the choice of the numerical method to use for the solution of the Maxwell equations is not a matter of preference, but a matter of necessity.
, in the presence of a metamaterial, the accuracy of a numerical method depends on its ability to accurately represent a high frequency field in the metamaterial region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite element method is not well suited to the solution of problems with effective models, while finite difference methods are.
the FDFD method can be used to simulate metamaterials without any concern.
finite difference frequency domains methods can be considered as a reliable tool to study metamaterials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
